chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who borrows a specific number of silver dirhams, then repays them with gold dinars by weight, knowing that the gold is heavier than what he borrowed, and he is pleased to give him the excess as a favor. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in it if there is no condition attached, and even if he gifted them all to him, it would be more appropriate.'

key_terms.شَرْطٌ: Condition (specifically a condition attached to the loan contract)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to repay a silver loan with heavier gold coins in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* clarifies the distinction between *qard* (loan) and *rib al-fadl* (excess in exchange) by permitting the repayment of silver dirhams with gold dinars by weight, provided the heavier weight is not a stipulated condition (*shart*) of the loan itself. Scholars note that if the borrower voluntarily gives more due to the weight difference, it is treated as a gift (*hibah*), avoiding the prohibition of riba; however, if the heavier weight is explicitly agreed upon as the repayment term, it constitutes riba. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the intentionality and contractual conditions in determining the validity of mixed-currency transactions.
